claims.claim: The repository worker dependency file, launcher authoritative commit, and runtime provenance tests bind exactly to AIOS-renew commit 59b31ede597d4a27b848771522672705a021abe4 and reject the previous or any alternate kernel commit.

Both documented Human surfaces expose exactly `REPAIR RUN-N-NNN` in addition to the existing RUN, FIX, and STATUS forms, with Codex fixed to executor codex and Antigravity fixed to executor antigravity.

The shared launcher parses a valid canonical failed RUN identifier for REPAIR, rejects missing or malformed REPAIR targets before kernel invocation, and does not treat REPAIR input as a TASK or finding id.

For each executor, one REPAIR request builds exactly one pinned-kernel command containing `repair FAILED_RUN_ID --executor EXECUTOR --repo REPO` and containing none of `--repair`, TASK id, finding id, failed-head, scope, constraints, instructions, or verification authority.
Codex and Antigravity REPAIR routing is executor-neutral and command-identical except for the explicit executor value; no surface can select, infer, reroute to, or substitute the other executor.

REPAIR uses the same exact dedicated pinned worker runtime as RUN/FIX/STATUS; normal REPAIR documentation and tests require no raw global `python -m aios_renew.operator repair` invocation and preserve existing deterministic bootstrap-host fallback behavior.
Any kernel or bootstrap failure returns failure after at most one admitted kernel invocation and performs no retry, reroute, fallback execution, publication, or worker-owned continuation.

A unique valid `AIOS REPAIR PASS` summary is parsed fail-closed, including exact TASK identity, failed RUN, failed head SHA, and candidate head SHA; malformed, duplicated, missing, or inconsistent REPAIR PASS summary fields are rejected rather than guessed.

On successful REPAIR the worker prints REVIEW_CANDIDATE_HEAD equal to the exact kernel head_sha and `NEXT: Review TASK-N in ChatGPT` using the exact kernel-rendered task field rather than deriving TASK-N from FAILED_RUN_ID.

Existing RUN TASK-N, FIX TASK-N FINDING-ID, and STATUS TASK-N behavior, strict PASS parsing, one-kernel-invocation rule, no-push rule, executor separation, bootstrap/provenance behavior, and current tests continue without semantic regression.

Documentation consistently describes REPAIR as a Human-authorized thin delegation to the pinned AIOS-renew kernel, with the kernel owning remote REPAIR lookup and all failure/repair semantics, and explicitly forbids the worker from inspecting or reconstructing repair lineage.
